name: Communication loss (two-way watchdog)
description: Unit carries 80 % load. A 80 ms link dropout must pass unnoticed; a 300 ms dropout must raise an alarm only; a 5 s loss must trip the controller after 10 failed polls (500 ms) and make the plant side close the fuel valve and open the breaker by itself. The trip stays latched after the link returns and clears only on an explicit reset, after which the start request is locked out until it is re-issued.

criteria.text: An 80 ms dropout raises no alarm
A 300 ms dropout raises the comms alarm
Neither short dropout trips the unit
The plant-side watchdog acts within 2 s of the loss
The controller trips within 2 s of the loss
Fuel flow is zero 2.5 s after the loss
Breaker is open 2.5 s after the loss
Speed stays below the overspeed trip level
Trip is still latched 3 s after the link returned (no auto-reset)
With the start request still held, the unit does not restart (cool-down only)

negative_tests.text: With both watchdogs removed the unit keeps running on stale commands through a 5 s loss of control.

hil.note: On the real rig the plant only sees what the controller managed to write. During a link loss the controller cannot write, so its alarm and trip are invisible to the plant until the link returns (and the comms alarm has already cleared by then).

skip.medium_alarm: the comms alarm lives only in the controller; it is visible on the STM32 serial log, not at the plant

ctrl_trip.text: The controller's trip is visible at the plant as soon as the link returns (by 38 s)

first_out_seen.text: The first-out reported after the link returns is communication loss (code 10)
